title: Touring the South with a mixed band
summary: Barnet says his mixed band had little trouble, mostly playing college dates and insisting on the mixed band in advance, while Willard recounts other bands' problems.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: They were afraid of the deep south at the time. They said they'd lose every -- and I never had that problem. I was down there with a mixed band and I didn't -- outside of the fact that the guys' accomodations at times were pretty raunchy, we never had any trouble on the job, anybody that took umbrage about it.

Really? Gee, because I've heard so many stories from other people that said they did. In fact Willie Smith told me once that when he was with Harry James they came into a town and they were met by a committee of

people who said, "We understand there's a nigger in this band." And so Harry James said, "Fine. Find him." And they couldn't find Willie. But they weren't going to let the band on because they heard that there was somebody in it.

Well, of course we didn't -- we didn't do very much touring in the south per se, outside of college dates. We got out of there. You know, we'd play the college dates and get out of there real fast. Because I was always fearful of it, but I'd always check with the college. I'd say, "Look, we have a mixed band and we either come that way or we don't come at all." "Oh, by all means," you know, so I don't know whether that forestalled anything. That couldn't have forestalled any of it, because people that act and feel that way, you're not going to say, no you don't.
Gee, well that's -- but you played like dances and things?
But only colleges? Did you play other things?
We'd have to play a few other dates to get to and get out, you know, in between, and it was -- I've had some people that were curious and asked dumb questions.
Well, like, "How do you guys feel, riding with them and being in their company?" I said, "How do you feel when you get in the elevator and there's a guy

running the elevator? You're in pretty close contact, you know. How do you feel about it? "Well, I never -- I didn't really mean anything." They actually -- they actually were -- there was more curiosity shown rather than venom.
Although I do know of people that have had trouble.
Yeah, I do too, so that's marvelous that you didn't. What years was it that you had mixed bands when you went south?
Well, I think Peanuts joined me in '41, either late '40 or -- yeah, in '40, I think it was he joined me, late '40 and '41, '42, '43. Those years. And '44.
